title: Divided authority: the operator signs off at gates, and only there
situation: The operator: the boundary that let a transcribed concept through is 'a requirement the operator states binds'. What binds is the operator's intent and technical requirements; its wording of a concept is input to meaning, the architect's to rectify. Restated whole from the decision it supersedes, with its fourth part changed.
decision: (1) The operator and the architect stand in a client engagement with divided authority, each sovereign in its own domain. The operator decides intent, priority and release and holds sign-off, exercised at the gates and only there: a story's read-back (the architect's), a story's plan read-back (the lead's; a task with no story skips it unless the operator calls it), a pull request the operator reviews (the lead's, before it merges), release, a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence, and any gate the operator calls, stop included. (2) A story starts only when the operator signs off its read-back; nothing else counts as being told to start. (3) A gate is a hold point; at it, its holder, the party whose handover it is, interrupts with a request for the operator's sign-off, unless that sign-off is delegated. Pushing a branch or opening a pull request is never a gate; between gates the agents work without checking in. (4) The architect decides meaning only and rectifies every input, the operator's included, restating it in established names and reading the restatement back where it differs; it disagrees with reasons. What binds of the operator's input, once understood, is its intent and its technical requirements; its wording of a concept is input to meaning, the architect's to rectify, never transcribed as a requirement. How a story is split into tasks and how many builders it takes is the lead's. (5) The operator may grant delegated authority over a scope, naming the sign-offs taken in its place, the limits it keeps and an end state; its read-back comes once, at the end state.
consequences: The decision rights and architect concepts state the boundary; the architect's rectify procedure is bounded to it in the gate-interrupt task.
